en.summary: Recent releases bring significant improvements to database connectivity and deployment workflows. Interactive authentication for Databricks eliminates the need for stored credentials, while Snowflake advanced capabilities support expands platform coverage. The new Automated deployment page streamlines release processes, and MCP tooling now enables AI-assisted migration testing and schema validation. Enhanced code review policies configuration and improved drift resolution workflows give teams better control over quality gates and production safety.

highlights: Databricks now supports interactive browser-based sign-in without requiring stored credentials
Databricks Lakehouse connections now support OAuth interactive sign-in through the browser
JDBC URLs can now be pasted directly from Snowflake without manual formatting corrections
New Databricks Lakebase property resolver enables interactive sign-in without storing credentials
Environment-specific plugin parameters can now be configured in TOML for flexible multi-environment deployments
Oracle deployment scripts can now preserve the original case of schema names
Object-level history now displays current branch, schema, and object type for better context
Log files are automatically cleaned up after 30 days to reduce disk usage
Oracle deployment scripts can now preserve the original case of schema names
New Flyway Report implementation is now enabled by default with improved performance
Flyway Insights publishing can now be configured directly from project settings
A search function has been added to code review settings for easier policy management
AI-generated migration descriptions are now shorter to prevent Windows path-length errors
Object level history now includes a diff settings button for easier comparison customization
Snapshot history feature is now supported on Snowflake for improved drift detection and rollback capabilities
Snapshots are now saved by default during deployment, enabling drift analysis and rollbacks without additional configuration
AI can now explain specific changes in object-level history to help teams understand schema evolution
Snowflake advanced capabilities are now available in public preview for enhanced platform support
Deploy tab now automatically reloads migrations when they're added or run elsewhere in the project
New MCP Test Migrate tool runs pending migration scripts against a shadow database to validate changes before deployment
MCP now supports 3-sided diff by creating a schema model checkpoint for comprehensive change analysis
Snowflake Postgres is now recognized as a distinct database type for better compatibility
Databricks connection dialog now includes dedicated fields for improved configuration clarity
Dry run reports now include a deployment overview table for better visibility into planned changes
Code analysis can now exclude specific rule groups using a built-in schemaModel profile
Docker provisioner now provides clearer error messages when Docker daemon is not running
Object level history is now enabled by default as a preview feature on Enterprise edition
Schema model page now alerts users when there are upstream changes in version control
Migrations page now shows connection errors instead of misleading 'no migrations found' messages
Comparison filters can now be configured for Databricks Lakebase projects
Debug logs now show final configuration parameters and their sources for easier troubleshooting
Dry run scripts are now more concise by removing unnecessary statements
Deploying to a non-empty target database now offers to baseline it automatically instead of failing
Flyway now automatically uses operating system proxy configuration for better enterprise network support
Snowflake parser now supports AGENT IF EXISTS clause for improved compatibility
Deployment review drawer now shows a dedicated summary after manual deployment
Provisioners now display documentation links in connection dialogs for easier setup
Code review policies can now be configured directly in Flyway Desktop instead of requiring external tools
CockroachDB is now provided as a standalone database module for better compatibility
New Automated deployment page is now available in public preview to streamline release workflows
Databricks Lakebase is now recognized as a supported database type in public preview
Snapshot history is now supported on Databricks for improved change tracking
Databricks Lakebase is now supported as a distinct database type with dedicated connection fields
Oracle can now add the ONLINE clause to index creation scripts for non-blocking operations
Oracle now supports an IncludeOnlineIndexCreation option for non-blocking index operations
New Flyway MCP server exposes development-time tools for AI agents to run Flyway commands and perform schema analysis
Guided shadow provisioning is now always available to Enterprise customers as a standard feature
PostgreSQL now supports a disable-constraints-for-static-data option for faster data loading
Databricks advanced capabilities support is now available in public preview
Smart Docker provisioner now reuses the build database container across Flyway commands to improve performance
Cassandra now uses Native Connectors mode by default for better performance
New check.driftResolutionFolder setting allows customization of where drift resolution scripts are generated
Advanced parameter check.driftResolutionFolder can now be configured for drift analysis operations
PostgreSQL filter UI now includes an option to filter across any object type
Flyway now warns when offline permits are due to expire within 30 days
PostgreSQL filter editor now allows multiple rules per object type for more flexible filtering patterns

de.summary: Aktuelle Releases bringen erhebliche Verbesserungen der Datenbankconnectivity und Deployment-Workflows. Interaktive Authentifizierung für Databricks eliminiert die Notwendigkeit für gespeicherte Anmeldedaten, während erweiterte Snowflake-Funktionen die Plattformunterstützung erweitern. Die neue Seite für automatisierte Bereitstellung optimiert Release-Prozesse, und MCP-Tools ermöglichen nun KI-gestützte Migrationstests und Schemavalidierung. Erweiterte Konfiguration von Code-Review-Richtlinien und verbesserte Drift-Resolution-Workflows geben Teams bessere Kontrolle über Quality Gates und Produktionssicherheit.

Databricks Lakehouse-Verbindungen unterstützen nun OAuth-interaktive Anmeldung über den Browser
JDBC-URLs können nun direkt aus Snowflake eingefügt werden, ohne manuelle Formatierungskorrektionen

Umgebungsspezifische Plugin-Parameter können nun in TOML für flexible Multi-Umgebungs-Deployments konfiguriert werden
Oracle-Deployment-Skripte können nun die ursprüngliche Groß- und Kleinschreibung von Schemanamen beibehalten
Objekthistorie auf Objektebene zeigt nun aktuellen Branch, Schema und Objekttyp für besseren Kontext an
Protokolldateien werden automatisch nach 30 Tagen gelöscht, um die Festplattennutzung zu reduzieren
